question: The pay of a Government Servant drawing pay of Rs. 18950 + 4800 from 1.7.2011 was reduced by two stages with effect from 1.9.2014 for a period of two years as a measure of penalty. It was ordered that the reduction would not have the effect of postponing his future increments and he will earn increments of pay during the period of reduction. Regulate his pay from 1.7.2011 to 1.7.2017.

A Government servant drawing the pay of Rs. 22440 (17640 + 4800) in the Pay Band plus Grade Pay of Rs. 9300 – 34800 + 4800 with effect from 1.7.2015 proceeded on extraordinary leave without medical Certificate for 30 days from 1.9.2015 and in continuation Earned Leave for 15 days. He was appointed to officiate on a regular basis in a higher post in the same pay band but with a grade pay of Rs 5400 with effect from 1.12.2015. He again proceeded on Extraordinary leave without medical certificate for 30 days from 1.6.2016 and in continuation Earned Leave for 31 days and Half Pay Leave for 92 days. After expiry of leave, he stood reverted to the lower post on 1.11.2016. He was again promoted to the same higher post in the same Pay Band plus Grade Pay of Rs 5400 on 1.4.2017. It was certified by the Competent Authority that he would have continued to officiate in the higher post up to 30.9.2016 but for his proceeding on leave. Regulate his Pay from time to time and fix his pay on 1.4.2017 and state when he will draw his next increment.

A Government servant drawing pay of Rs. 18220 + 4200 in the Pay Band and Grade Pay of Rs. 9300 – 34800 + 4200 was sanctioned House Building Advance of Rs. 3,00,000 which was paid in two instalments in October 2015 and March 2016. The advance was to be repaid in 120 instalments of Rs. 2500 each. Rate of interest 9.5% per annum. Recovery of the advance commenced from the pay of August 2016. If the Official wants to repay the advance with interest on 27.11.2017, calculate the amount payable by the Official.

Calculate the standard Licence fee for a Government residential building occupied by a Government Officer from the following data: Cost of land 25000, Cost of Preparation of site 3000, Cost of building 50000, Cost of fencing 1500, Cost of attached garage 3500, Electric Installation 2000, Water installation 1400, Rate of Interest 4%, Rate of ordinary and special repairs 1½%, Municipal Tax 1200 p.a, Tools and plant charged direct to work but not included in any of the above 1300. Work out the licence fee payable by the officer occupying the above building for November 2017 from the following particulars: Pay Rs. 25050, Grade Pay Rs.7600, Special Pay Rs. 550, Dearness allowance 139% of Pay + GP = Rs. 45384, Non Recurring Fee Rs. 500, The prescribed flat rate licence fee of the building is Rs. 1099 pm.

With reference to Rule 77-A (General instructions for handling cash) and other relevant provisions under Central Treasury Rules Vol – I, give your comments on the Cash Book entry for the month of October 2017 done by the Cashier of Directorate of Local Administration Department (copy provided in separate sheet).
With the help of a diagram/ flow chart discuss the divisions of Government Accounts as provided in Account Code Vol – I.

From the following transactions of Executive Engineer, Building Division for the month of June 2017, prepare the monthly Account in Form 80. [Detailed transactions including opening balance, cash receipts (rent from circuit house Rs. 13000, rent of government residential buildings Rs. 21000, sale of tender forms Rs. 3000), earnest money from contractors Rs. 26000, deposits for works Rs. 640000, cheque from another PWD division Rs. 210000, payments in cash (advertisement Rs. 9000, freight Rs. 12000, conveyance Rs. 3000), construction work Rs. 400000, rent of hired buildings Rs. 1300000, refund of security deposit Rs. 40000, work outlay on deposit works Rs. 360000, departmental charges including establishment 22½%, tools & plant ¾%, audit & account ¼%, pensionary ¼%, purchase of office furniture Rs. 26000, remittances into bank Rs. 913000, cement received through DGS&D Rs. 430000, steel issued from stock Rs. 120000, unclaimed deposits Rs. 220000].

From the particulars given below, calculate – (i) Qualifying service for pension, (ii) Pension (iii) Retirement Gratuity and (iv) Family pension admissible to an Officer of the Government of Mizoram who retired on 30.6.2017 on attaining the age of superannuation. [Details: Date of Birth 10.6.1957, Joined service as Clerk 25.8.1984, Promoted as Section Officer 3.11.1992, Promoted as Accounts Officer 10.2.2015, Drawing pay Rs. 22010 pm from 1.7.2015 with DNI on 1.7.2016, Joined MSACS on deputation 1.9.2016 with 10% deputation allowance, Rejoined parent office 1.2.2017 as Group A post with pay Rs. 25150, Transfer in 1997 with 25 days excess joining time treated as dies non, Various spells of leave including half pay leave (17.3.1991-28.5.1991), earned leave (16.6.2001-14.7.2001), extraordinary leave (2.1.2004-26.3.2004), extraordinary leave on medical certificate (4.10.2007-15.12.2007)].

Post the following transactions in the Cash Book of the Executive Engineer, Hmuifang Division (Form provided in separate sheet), for the month of October 2017 and close the Cash Book giving an analysis of the Cash Balance. [Details: Opening balance including notes and coins Rs. 3250 (with counterfeit notes Rs. 250), service postage stamps Rs. 150, revenue stamps Rs. 10000, deposit-at-call receipt Rs. 1000, refund of festival advance Rs. 5000, demand draft Rs. 2000; Cheque No. 069 for contractor for government staff quarters (estimate Rs. 1300000, work value Rs. 40000, recoveries including security deposit Rs. 6000, material supplied Rs. 2000, hire charges Rs. 1000, tools lost Rs. 100); Cheque No. 071 for cash replenishment Rs. 5000; Earnest money from contractor B (rejected tender) Rs. 10000; Cash challan from SDO Rs. 1000; Temporary imprest account (muster roll Rs. 1500, coolie Rs. 250, amount lost Rs. 250); Grant of permanent imprest Rs. 2000; Dishonoured demand draft Rs. 5000; Service stamps payment Rs. 2000; Treasury remittance Rs. 8000].
